new_sources.summary: Brady argues that suffering is essential to the development and expression of moral virtue, and also the executive virtue of wisdom. He starts by considering the ‘virtue solution’ to the problem of evil, and raises objections to this general line. But he then illustrates the importance of suffering for moral virtue by considering Buddhist thought, and contemporary empirical work. Brady goes on to argue that there are good philosophical and psychological reasons to suppose that suffering is essential for wisdom. Suffering motivates the kind of reflection that is needed for evaluative understanding, whilst at the same time reflection on suffering adversity is positively correlated with wisdom.
new_sources.title: Suffering, Morality, and Wisdom
